eligibility_evidence.text: Camden High Risk Podiatrist An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced and highly motivated High-Risk Podiatrist to join our service in a permanent 3 days (22.5 hrs) post, working primarily at University College London Hospital (UCLH). This is a rewarding role at the forefront of specialist podiatric care, where you will play a pivotal role in preventing limb loss, enhancing quality of life, and delivering outstanding outcomes for patients with complex high-risk foot conditions. As a senior clinician, you are required bring extensive Band 7-level expertise in the management of diabetes-related foot disease, vascular complications of the lower limb, and complex wound care. Working as an integral member of podiatry and multidisciplinary diabetes and vascular teams, you will provide and lead on delivering care, assessment, treatment, and ongoing management for patients with highly complex needs in an acute hospital setting. This role provides an excellent opportunity to support and influence patient care across the wider service, working closely with community podiatry colleagues, offering specialist guidance, advice, to manage complex foot conditions and deliver high-quality patient care. A key aspect of the role is developing others through, supervision, education, coaching, and mentorship of staff, students, and apprentices, helping to build skills, confidence, and future expertise within the podiatry workforce. To provide specialist footcare for patient with complex high-risk foot problems. This includes diabetes patients with acute and chronic foot wounds, patients with neuropathic and vascular complications, patient with foot complications who are immunosuppressed and patients who have poor tissue viability, vulnerable patients and patients with complex mental health issues. The post holder will be clinically accountable and responsible for treatment of the high-risk caseload working autonomously as well as work as part of the multidisciplinary team. The post requires accepting emergency referrals from GPs, community podiatrists, and other health professionals and will provide responsive specialist care. A need for education and up-skilling of clinical and care staff working with diabetic care. There will be also be a responsibility for patient education. There’s a place for you at CNWL We’re passionate about delivering first-class patient-centred, safe and effective care, whether it is in a hospital setting, in a community clinic or in the patient’s own home. Patients are at the heart of everything we do. Providing top quality care depends on our ability to employ the best people. We’re always looking to recruit outstanding people who will go the extra mile to support our patients, colleagues, teams and the Trust. With every new employee we’re hoping to find our future leaders and we’ll support our staff by providing opportunities to develop your career. To work in accordance with College of Podiatry and Health and Care Professions Council Code of Professional Conduct including scope of professional practice. To assess, manage and treat high risk complex caseload consisting of patients with: acute and chronic diabetic foot problems, pre and post operative amputations wounds and acute and chronic neuropathic, vascular foot/lower limb problems To use clinical reasoning skill in the assessment, diagnoses and formulating treatment plans of patients with a variety of high-risk foot problems and other medical conditions To provide podiatry care including wound care for patients with musculoskeletal conditions. To use clinical reasoning skill in the assessment, diagnoses and formulating treatment plans of patients with a variety of high risk foot problems and medical conditions ability to cope with unpredictable work patterns as necessitated in acute wound care clinics To recognise and request when diagnostics are required and make onward referrals as needed. To recognise the need, undertake and understand the result of investigations such as microbiology, x-ray, and scans and respond appropriately. To have highly developed physical skills, precision hand/eye co-ordination which involves highly skilled debridement techniques of acute/chronic, neuropathic and ischaemic wounds, often for prolonged periods. Develop and contribute to the care and management of complex wounds and lower limb complications To apply and practice principles of wound management Have advance knowledge of dressing and there modes of action and appropriate indications of their use in wound care. To have a good working knowledge of biomechanics and its role wound care and basic musculoskeletal problems. To take the clinical diabetes/high risk foot specialist role within the multidisciplinary diabetes foot team. To promote multidisciplinary team working. To provide diabetes and other high risk foot care within community, specialist clinics, secondary care, wards and in patient/nursing/residential homes, this will be based on agreed referral criteria and ensuring patients are not placed at risk. To take direct referrals from GP; community podiatry and community nursing in the hospital setting and providing rapid access and expert clinical advise and intervention based on agreed referral criteria. To provide podiatry care including wound care for patients with musculoskeletal conditions To have highly developed physical skills, precision hand/eye co-ordination which involves highly skilled debridement techniques of acute/chronic, neuropathic and ischaemic wounds, often for prolonged periods. To line manage staff providing them with regular supervision and being available when they need. To take an active role in education of staff, students and apprentices. eligibility_evidence.text: About us auticon is an IT Consultancy and Social Enterprise whose mission is to address the inequalities in employment for neurodivergent adults. We aim to provide long-term career opportunities for autistic adults, who we employ as IT and Data Consultants. They then deliver high-quality services to our clients. If you’re not familiar with how IT Consultancies operate, read more on our blog. Registering your interest and how we recruit We always want to hear from autistic people with strong tech and data skills who would like to join us. We recruit new Consultants based on available project opportunities, aligning our hiring needs with client demand. As a result, we encourage interested candidates to register their interest and complete a few initial questions to determine whether they meet our general criteria. Registering your interest is not an application for a specific role; instead, it allows you to share your CV and become part of our talent pool. Once in the talent pool, we continually review your skillset against client opportunities and initiate our recruitment process when a suitable position becomes available. Find out more about our recruitment process on our website: auticon – Careers UK. Because our hiring is demand-driven, timelines are variable depending on client needs. During your time in the talent pool, we encourage you subscribe to our quarterly Careers Newsletter and share any updates with us. What to expect as an auticon Consultant As an auticon Consultant, you become a permanent employee of auticon, but most of your day-to-day work will be with one of our clients. You’ll add skills and expertise to the client’s team or project. Most of our clients are large multinational organisations who require expertise in areas such as: Data analysis Data visualisation Data engineering Cyber security Machine learning or AI You get the chance to work on interesting assignments with our clients, whilst still having all the support of being an auticon employee. When you’re between projects, your employment with us continues. This means you receive your salary and all the ongoing benefits of being an auticon employee such as our valuable coaching provision, whilst we support you to further develop your skills. Visit our blog to learn more about the value of the coaching we provide. What we offer A salary of £29,000 – £40,000 (normally £29,000 – £32,000 for Consultants with lower levels of work experience or £32,000 – £40,000 for Consultants with more relevant work experience or practical application of skills via a PhD, for example) Permanent contract that includes valuable autism-tailored benefits, such as ongoing assistance from a dedicated Coach who provides practical and emotional support to help you thrive in your role 25 days annual leave, plus bank holidays Private health insurance package Friendly and productive work environment where reasonable adjustments are understood and encouraged Personal development with fully funded courses What we’re looking for Essential Criteria – to be considered, you must have: Evidence that you are in the process of obtaining an autism diagnosis OR evidence you already have a diagnosis OR alternative documentation to evidence autism Right to work in the UK The ability to commute to central London on a regular basis, around 2-3 times per week (As a responsible employer, we’re aware of the sensory and emotional impact of longer commutes. We consider a reasonable commute to be no longer than 1.5 hours each way) Demonstrable proficiency in Python, including the use of relevant libraries (NumPy, pandas, etc.). For example, a PCAP certification or equivalent, professional experience or meaningful academic experience. Experience in: Using data analysis tools (e.g. Power BI, Tableau) Processing large data sets accurately An interest and willingness to upskill in Artificial Intelligence Desirable Criteria - please note that you don’t need to meet all, or any, of the criteria listed below in order to apply: Certification in one of the major cloud services (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud Platform, etc.) Cyber security skills, experience or certification (e.g. CompTIA) Some relevant work experience, or equivalent practical application of skills through a PhD A recognised security clearance or the willingness to undertake national security vetting (e.g. SC, DV) so that you can work on projects with our public sector clients. This requires you to have been a UK resident for 5 years (you can find an overview of what UK Govt Security Vetting involves on the Cabinet Office’s YouTube channel) Inclusion Statement We’re committed to equality of opportunity in all areas of our work. You’ll be treated in a fair and equal manner regardless of your gender, marital status, race, religion, age, disability or sexual orientation. We welcome applications from a diverse range of backgrounds, including people from diverse ethnic and cultural backgrounds, people with disabilities, people from diverse educational and socio-economic backgrounds and people who identify as LGBTQIA+. Inclusion is at the heart of everything we do at auticon and that starts with our recruitment process, which has been designed to make you feel comfortable to be your authentic self. As a Disability Confident Leader, we’re committed to providing applicants with any reasonable adjustments or accommodations needed. Therefore, please let us know if you require any reasonable adjustments as part of the recruitment process. Location: SE London, London. Hybrid Permanent Full time

eligibility_evidence.text: Recruitment Consultant (London) Organisation: GoodPeople Reports to: Delivery Lead Location: Somerset House, London, hybrid, with a minimum of one day per week in our London office and regular in-person work with employers, partners and candidates. The role will also involve travel to education partners, community venues, construction sites and other delivery locations as required. Contract: Permanent, full-time, 37.5 hours per week Salary: £32,000 to £40,000 base depending on experience, plus target-based commission, with OTE of £45,000+ If you can source, engage and place great people, and you want the work to mean something, this is your chance to do it with real purpose behind it. We're a fast-growing social enterprise connecting purposeful employers to diverse local talent at scale. Think of us as a recruitment agency with a mission: we combine tech-enabled support with in-person delivery to get local people into good work across the built environment, construction, green skills and infrastructure. Our client base spans developers, utilities companies, housing associations and major contractors, through to SMEs. The built environment, infrastructure and net zero sectors face some of the biggest skills shortages in the country, alongside a once-in-a-generation pipeline of work that needs local people to deliver it. We're looking for a Recruitment Consultant who can build relationships on both sides of the market. You'll source, screen and place candidates against live roles, and you'll be just as comfortable talking to employers about their hiring needs as you are supporting a jobseeker into work. You'll work closely with community partners, including training providers, colleges, charities and job centres, to reach people traditional recruitment can overlook, using our tools and platform to deliver at volume. The role As a Recruitment Consultant, you'll take ownership of qualified employer accounts and live vacancies, using a range of routes to source, support and place local candidates. You'll manage recruitment activity from employer handover through to placement, keep a consistently strong pipeline moving and build employer relationships that lead to further hiring opportunities. You'll work closely with training providers, community partners and other networks to reach candidates traditional recruitment can miss, using our tools and platform to deliver efficiently and at scale. You'll be part of a delivery team led by our Delivery Lead, with clear support, shared standards and a strong focus on quality and outcomes. Key activities Candidate sourcing and screening: Identify, attract and engage suitable candidates through job boards, partner referrals, direct sourcing and our own pipeline, and assess their skills, experience and suitability against live vacancies. Job advertising and marketing: Write clear, compelling adverts and promote opportunities across appropriate platforms and networks, including in-person job fairs and community events. Client relationship management: Take ownership of employer accounts, build relationships, manage the recruitment process, maintain strong communication, provide consultative market insight and identify further hiring needs. Candidate support and sessions: Provide tailored one-to-one and group support to jobseekers, including employability sessions, CV and interview preparation, and confidence building. Process improvement and automation: Find ways to streamline recruitment delivery, including using digital tools and automation to improve efficiency, consistency and impact. Record keeping and reporting: Maintain accurate records of employers, vacancies, candidates and applications, manage pipelines effectively and contribute to agreed placement targets. What we're looking for Demonstrated experience in a recruitment or employment support role, with the ability to deliver job outcomes at scale A track record of working at pace and consistently delivering above target Experience sourcing, screening and progressing candidates against live vacancies Confidence building and managing employer relationships and recruitment processes Experience supporting entry-level jobseekers or people who may face barriers to work, including providing careers advice Strong organisation and attention to detail across multiple vacancies and candidate processes Confidence using recruitment systems, data and digital tools, and the ability to establish and optimise processes A collaborative approach and the ability to work closely with colleagues and partners Willingness to attend our London office at least one day per week and travel to work in person with partners, employers and candidates A genuine interest in community, equality and impact Desirable Experience of 360 recruitment, including both repeat and new business Experience working across construction, the built environment, infrastructure or green skills Experience delivering employability support, workshops or candidate preparation Experience using technology to semi-automate processes Knowledge of inclusive recruitment and the barriers faced by people from underrepresented communities What we offer A meaningful role connecting people to good work A collaborative, values-driven team with clear support and development A base salary of £32,000 to £40,000 depending on experience A target-based commission scheme that rewards placements above target, with enhanced commission for developing employer accounts and securing additional vacancies Hybrid working, with at least one day per week in our London office 25 days' holiday pro rata A yearly flexible training and development budget Private healthcare provision and 24/7 access to a GP The eligibility_evidence.text: Your new company My client is an award-winning sustainability & environmental consultancy with a strong reputation for delivering innovative environmental solutions across the natural & built environment. Their multidisciplinary teams work collaboratively across ecology, biodiversity, ESG, planning, net zero, and environmental disciplines to help create more sustainable and resilient places. As part of continued growth, they are seeking a Senior Ecologist to join their London office. This is an excellent opportunity to work on a diverse portfolio of projects across residential, commercial, infrastructure and mixed-use developments while helping to deliver measurable biodiversity enhancements and positive environmental outcomes. The organisation places sustainability at the heart of everything they do and offers a genuinely collaborative culture where employees are empowered to develop their careers and make a meaningful impact. Your new role As a Consultant Ecologist, you will play a key role in delivering ecology and biodiversity projects from inception through to completion. Working alongside experienced technical specialists, planners and sustainability professionals, you'll provide high-quality ecological advice to a varied client base. Your responsibilities will include: Undertaking ecological surveys and assessments, including UKHab and protected species surveys, ecological impact assessments etc. Producing and reviewing a range of technical reports, including Preliminary Ecological Appraisals (PEAs), Ecological Impact Assessments (EcIAs), Biodiversity Net Gain (BNG) assessments, Habitat Regulations Assessments (HRAs), and protected species reports. Undertaking and managing ecological surveys and coordinating subcontractors where required. Using biodiversity metrics and GIS tools to support habitat assessments and BNG delivery. Managing project budgets, programmes and client relationships. Mentoring and supporting junior ecologists within the team. Working collaboratively with a wider multidisciplinary team to deliver integrated sustainability solutions. You'll primarily be working on strategic masterplans, conducting ecological and UKHab surveys that feed into wider Biodiversity Net-Gain and Natural Capital projects, whilst primarily project managing. Otherwise, they work on planning projects for the residential, education, accommodation and health sectors. They do not work on infrastructure; rail, road projects. You'll be working with some very well recognised individuals in the industry who are working at a high level into things such as: IEMA steering groups, Natural England advisory boards, writing codes of conduct in relation to carbon calculations and other research based work. What you'll need to succeed Essential: A degree in Ecology, Environmental Science, Biology or a related discipline. Consultancy experience delivering ecological projects within the UK. Strong knowledge of UK ecological legislation, planning policy and best practice guidance. Experience producing ecological reports including PEAs, EcIAs and BNG assessments. Experience coordinating field surveys and ecological inputs into planning applications. Excellent project management and client-facing skills. Strong report writing, communication and organisational skills. A passion for delivering positive outcomes for nature and biodiversity. Full UK Driving license. Desirable: MSc qualification. Membership of CIEEM, ideally working towards Chartership or an equivalent professional accreditation. Experience using GIS software and Biodiversity Net Gain metrics. Protected species licenses and or tree climbing & aerial rescue. FISC 3 or above certification. RCA qualification. Experience mentoring junior consultants. What you'll get in return Competitive salary: £30,000 - £36,000 (DoE) Discretionary annual bonus. Hybrid working arrangements with flexibility around office and home working. Part-time options. Flexible working hours. Private medical care - depending on level and position. Enhanced pension contributions. 25 days annual leave increasing with tenure, and the ability to carry up to 5 over to the following year. Ongoing training and professional development opportunities. Clear career progression within a growing ecology and sustainability team. Work mobile phone. Mileage and expenses paid. Enhanced family-friendly policies. Cycle-to-work scheme. Two paid volunteer days p/year and opportunities to support environmental initiatives. Comprehensive wellbeing and lifestyle benefits package (eye tests, vaccines etc.) The opportunity to work on exciting projects that contribute towards biodiversity enhancement and sustainable development. Low utilisation target across the team, they aren't all about chargeable time! What you need to do now If you're interested in this role, click 'apply now' to forward an up-to-date copy of your CV, or call us now. If this job isn't quite right for you but you are looking for a new position, please contact us for a confidential discussion on your career. Hays Specialist Recruitment Limited acts as an employment agency for permanent recruitment and employment business for the supply of temporary workers. By applying for this job you accept the T&C's, Privacy Policy and Disclaimers which can be found at hays.co.uk. Hybrid Permanent Full time

eligibility_evidence.text: Associate Recruitment Consultant - White Collar Property Services - London £27k- £30k per annum DOE + OTE Earnings Daniel Owen is looking for an ambitious Associate Recruitment Consultant to join our London team, an excellent opportunity for someone looking to build a long-term career in recruitment. Working within our White Collar Property Services division, you will work across a range of disciplines, including the social housing sector, building strong relationships with candidates and helping clients secure the talent they need. Your Impact as an Associate Recruitment Consultant Candidate Relationships: Not just over the phone, but face-to-face, you'll identify, develop and maintain candidate relationships. Talent Sourcing: Seek out skilled individuals with the right qualifications, experience and career goals for permanent opportunities. Recruitment Support: Provide recruitment and administrative support, including maintaining databases and candidate profiles. Permanent Recruitment: Support the team with permanent white collar construction recruitment, helping to match high-quality candidates to suitable roles. Client Relationships: Build strong working relationships with existing clients, supporting repeat business and long-term partnerships. The Ideal Candidate Will Be A Proven Professional: Whether your background is in recruitment, sales, customer service or another target-driven environment, you know how to build relationships, get results and deliver a high-quality service. Motivated and Ambitious: You are driven to succeed, keen to develop your recruitment career and excited by the opportunity to influence your earnings with your work. Excellent Communicator: You're a brilliant communicator, both face-to-face and email, with the confidence to build strong relationships with candidates, clients and colleagues. Adaptable: You thrive in a fast-paced recruitment environment and can confidently pivot when priorities change. Organised: You are able to plan, structure, and manage tasks efficiently, staying organised to meet deadlines, support live vacancies, and achieve goals. Career-Focused: You are looking for more than a job; you want a long-term career where you can grow, develop and be in more control of your earnings within a supportive team. Our Benefits Are Second to None Top Tier Holiday Allowance: Increasing holiday allowance for the first five years, reaching 28 days, plus your birthday off and an additional day for charitable endeavours. Health and Wellbeing: Private healthcare through Vitality, contributory pension and life assurance. Director Incentives: Quarterly lunch incentives and personal treat vouchers. Loyalty Rewards: Additional holiday entitlement and bonus payments linked to service milestones. Annual Reward Trips: Multiple company trips throughout the year, with previous destinations including Marbella, Prague and Portugal. Learning and Growth: Access to the Daniel Owen Academy, featuring a structured 12-week training programme alongside one-to-one coaching and ongoing development. Financial Wellbeing Support: Access to professional financial guidance through our partnership with One Financial. Fast-Track Career Development: Our directors all climbed the ladder from within, as it's important for clear progression to be visible and achievable. Who Are We? For over 40 years, Daniel Owen has been a leading specialist recruiter within the built environment, recognised for our honest approach, strong relationships and commitment to developing our people. We believe recruitment is about people first. We invest heavily in training, reward success and provide the support needed for individuals to build long-term careers. As we continue to grow, there has never been a better time to join our team and make a real impact. Ready to Take the Next Step? Apply today to start your recruitment career with Daniel Owen. If you would like a confidential conversation about life at Daniel Owen, our Talent Acquisition team would be delighted to hear from you.. Permanent Full time

eligibility_evidence.text: Entry Level Recruitment Consultant London - Hays Recruitment We are seeking a sales-driven Entry Level Recruitment Consultant to join our flagship London office in our Professional Services Recruitment team. As an Entry Level Recruitment Consultant, your primary focus will be to develop and nurture relationships within organisations across London. You will be conducting business development (sales calls) to seek out and meet with Recruitment teams, Directors, line managers, and other key stakeholders. As an Entry Level Recruitment Consultant, you will be recruiting the best and most experienced candidates for roles across a professional sector. This is a sales based role where you will enjoy commission alongside your base salary with the potential to earn £32,000 - £40,000 in your first year. Your new team This is an opportunity for a trainee Recruitment Consultant join one of Hays' longest standing business areas with a strong client base and job flow. We offer a collaborative and inclusive environment ensuring you are set-up to succeed whilst being surrounded by expertise. Our London office is in the heart of the city and home to 300 ambitious sales driven consultants who work hard and celebrate success. Hays is the largest specialist recruiter globally and a multi award winning business covering 22 areas of recruitment across over 80 offices in the UK. We are professional, people centric and proud to be positively impacting our local people and businesses with the work we do. Your new role The responsibilities of an Entry level Recruitment Consultant include: * Making cold calls and sales calls to prospective clients to sell our services * Developing and maintaining strong relationships with organisations and key decision makers. * Actively engaging with face-to-face meetings with in-house recruitment professionals, directors, and line managers. * Sourcing, screening and recruiting top-tier candidates for roles. * Draft reports, ensure compliance, and participate in internal projects. * Working to daily targets and KPIs to achieve your monetary goals We pride ourselves in hiring the very best talent in the recruitment space and therefore you will need to meet the following criteria to apply: * A genuine drive to work in a sales environment - our best people are motivated to work to targets and go the extra mile for clients and candidates * The ability to communicate like a professional in the workplace * An individual who is resilient and not afraid of challenges * Has a good understanding of what 360 recruitment is and is passionate about pursuing a career within recruitment What you'll get in return Hays is a multi-award winning employer and we believe as part of the employee and employer deal, we can give you a career with unrivalled progression. Our culture is a reason why so many of our people choose to stay and grow their careers with Hays. Our colleagues describe our culture as 'high energy', 'inclusive', and 'great people' with a 'growth mindset'. In addition, you will enjoy: * Uncapped individual commission paid upon invoice every 4 weeks * Regular performance-based incentive programmes including all-expense paid international trips * A culture underpinned with trust, which is based on expertise, training, collaboration, inclusivity and doing the right thing * Industry-leading learning and development to maximise your performance and advance your career every step of the way * A global brand with established PSL agreements and warm client relationships * An adult approach to working with hybrid working models and flexible working hours * The opportunity to work in any of our 32 other countries through our global mobility offering * Diverse range of employee support networks, wellbeing initiatives and wider benefits We know talented people want to work with the best: people, brand, tools, technology and infrastructure. They also want career development. Our culture is shaped and created by these features. We also know our people want to do interesting and meaningful work, increasingly in an organisation that is purpose led. This is demonstrated in the work we have done through our commitment to DE&I, Net Zero and our global volunteering and fundraising programme, 'Helping for your tomorrow'. What to do next Please apply now to become the next Senior Recruitment Consultant or for more information on our roles. Life at Hays presents the opportunity for growth, varied career paths, exciting challenges and a culture of inclusion that celebrates diversity. As a committed Disability Confident employer, if you're thinking of a new tomorrow for your career, whatever your background, let's work together to create it! At Hays, we share a passion for creating a culture where there are opportunities for our people to flourish and succeed, whatever your background. We know that diversity of perspective and an inclusive approach, which encourages those experiences and views to be heard, is great for business and therefore your career with us.. Permanent Full time

eligibility_evidence.text: New Business Recruitment Consultant Self-employed opportunity for experienced recruiters | This is a Remote, Home-based opportunity. Not office-based. TPJ Recruit is expanding and seeking motivated, results-driven New Business Recruitment Consultants to join our growing team. This is a self-employed opportunity for an experienced recruiter who can win new clients, build lasting relationships and deliver permanent recruitment placements across Logistics, Transport and Driving, or other sectors where you can demonstrate strong success. You will manage the full 360 recruitment process, from securing new business and understanding client requirements through to sourcing, screening, interviewing and placing candidates. You will be expected to develop a deep understanding of each client’s business, identify opportunities and maintain excellent service standards throughout the recruitment cycle. This role is best suited to a disciplined, commercially focused recruiter who is confident working independently from home, can generate new business consistently and wants the flexibility and earning potential of a self-employed model. Job details Job title: New Business Recruitment Consultant Location: Remote, home-based Engagement type: Self-employed for the first 6 months* of service Commission: 50% of everything you bill during the self-employed period Sector focus: Logistics, Transport and Driver etc; Successful new-business winners with permanent placements from other sectors will be welcomed What we offer We offer experienced self-employed recruitment consultants the opportunity to retain a higher percentage of their billings than in a traditional employed recruitment role. During the initial self-employed period, you earn 50% of everything you bill. How it works For example, if your current employed recruiter role pays £30,000 basic salary plus 10% commission, billing £100,000 per year would generate approximately £40,000 in annual earnings. By contrast, billing £100,000 per year with TPJ Recruit on a 50% commission basis would generate approximately £50,000 in annual earnings, giving you a clear opportunity to increase your income while building something for yourself. ·Work in any permanent recruitment sector where you have proven experience, strong market knowledge and the confidence to generate new business. ·Join a business that values experienced, driven recruiters who can demonstrate a professional, disciplined and success-fueled work ethic. ·Focus on winning clients and making placements while we support back-office administration, including payroll and invoice chasing, etc. Flexibility to suit your lifestyle As a self-employed consultant, you can choose your own hours and work from home. This opportunity is ideal for someone who values flexibility, can stay productive without daily office supervision and is motivated by uncapped earning potential. Earnings: Uncapped and directly linked to your dedication, activity and billing performance. Main duties and responsibilities ·Source and secure new clients with the potential for multiple or frequent permanent placements. ·Liaise with clients regularly to understand their recruitment needs and prioritise your activity. ·Source suitable candidates for current and future vacancies. ·Write and publish professional job advertisements that attract relevant candidates. ·Develop and manage candidate relationships within your specialist market. ·Qualify candidate suitability for current and future vacancies through effective questioning, screening and referencing. ·Maintain and develop client relationships to deliver excellent service and maximise future business opportunities. ·Support the wider team by sharing market insight and identifying opportunities to generate revenue. ·Manage the recruitment process from start to finish for both clients and candidates. ·Handle client and candidate queries professionally, including objection handling and issue resolution. ·Manage placed candidates’ contracts and support the ongoing progression of live placements. ·Keep accurate records in line with recruitment legislation and company processes. ·Maintain accurate paperwork, system notes and CRM records, including candidate right-to-work information. ·Attend client site visits when required; you will therefore need access to a reliable car. *Review after 6 months After successfully operating for 6 months as a self-employed New Business Recruitment Consultant, you may choose to continue on a self-employed basis or be considered for a permanent employed position. Potential employed package after the initial 6 months ·£35,000 annual salary. ·20% commission paid on billed client invoices. For example, billing £100,000 would generate £20,000 commission, giving approximate annual earnings of £55,000+. ·Additional annual bonus for meeting and exceeding billed revenue targets. ·20 days’ annual paid leave plus England bank holidays, increasing by one additional day each year. ·Extra paid holiday during the Christmas and New Year shutdown. ·Company pension. ·Continued home working, reducing time spent commuting. ·Career progression opportunities. Please only apply if you have relevant new business recruitment experience. Applications that do not demonstrate this experience are unlikely to be progressed. We look forward to receiving your current, relevant and up-to-date CV. A supporting letter will strengthen your application. Please highlight the sectors where you have successfully won new business and explain why you should be considered for this opportunity. Please note that, due to the volume of applications, if you have not heard from us within 7 days, you should consider your application unsuccessful.. On-site Contract Full time

eligibility_evidence.text: Job Description Maven is looking for a Production & Operations Coordinator to join our London team. This is a broad, hands-on generalist role suited to someone who wants exposure across operations management, production coordination, business affairs administration, and film library oversight at a small independent company. This role reports to our VP, Production & Operations, Sophia Pedlow, and is primarily a support and administration role with opportunity to grow into more independent ownership over time. This role suits someone who is deeply organized, comfortable wearing multiple hats, and excited by the idea of understanding how an entire independent production company runs - not just how a single film gets made. Job Responsibilities Team Coordination - Track next steps and deliverables against project plans and budgets - Coordinate external meetings, including pitches with buyers and talent - Support the team in orchestrating weekly meetings as well as semi-annual staff performance reviews and annual company strategy offsites - Handle day-to-day office administration (phones, mail, filing, physical and digital organization) Finance & Business Affairs - Maintain the company database of projects, agreements, and contractual obligations - Support deal and contract administration and tracking - Help manage day-to-day relationships with key vendors and service providers - Facilitate bill, vendor, and contractor payment processing - File monthly invoices and receipts for the bookkeeping team - Implement staff expense tracking in line with company policy - Assist with research on the financial viability of projects under consideration Production Support - Perform production coordination duties as needed across pre-production, principal photography, and post-production - Support timely delivery of finished productions to distributors Library Oversight - Review and file sales, distribution, and collection account reports for the film library - Liaise with distributors and guilds to help ensure library compliance - Coordinate with collection account agents on compliance and timely payment processing - Help prepare stakeholder reports on released library titles for partners, investors, and producers About Maven Maven Screen Media is an independent development and production company dedicated to producing multi-platform film and television content while increasing representation for women in front of and behind the camera. We are a small but mighty full-service team, with a transatlantic footprint via offices in London and New York. Trudie Styler leads Maven’s global creative strategy whilst also Directing and producing key pictures. Celine Rattray oversees Maven’s global output, under which sits Anna Smith Tenser (Chief Content Officer) who oversees Maven’s slate across UK and Europe, and Jenny Halper (EVP, Head of Creative) who manages the US slate. Georgie Mullock serves as Jr Development Executive across the slate. Sophia Pedlow manages global finance, business affairs and operations for the company alongside production oversight.. eligibility_evidence.text: This role is offered on a 6‑9 month fixed‑term contract, with a salary of £28k–£30K pro‑rata. A proactive HR role in a mission-driven nursery group. Are you organised, curious, and love making things run smoothly behind the scenes? At the London Early Years Foundation (LEYF), we have 43 nurseries across London on a mission to ensure all children get the best start in life. As a charitable social enterprise, we put people before profit - and our People team plays a vital role in supporting our nurseries to make this happen. As our People Operations Administrator, you’ll play an important part supporting HR queries and processes across our nurseries and central office teams. Whether working with nursery managers, responding to our colleague’s HR questions or spotting ways to improve how we work, this is more than admin - you’ll be enabling our teams to focus on changing early years education across London. A Bit About the Role “You’ll be central in ensuring the smooth running of our HR operations to keep LEYF focused on what matters most - supporting London’s children.” As part of our People Operations Team, you’ll play an important role in supporting over 1,000 colleagues across our nurseries and Central Office. Whether you’re answering a question about policies, preparing starter lists, implementing workflows in our HRIS, or spotting ways to improve how we do things, every task you take on will help us achieve our mission. What we do matters because our people rely on timely, professional, and clear answers they can trust. You’ll bring your HR experience and be ready to keep learning. Your ability to deliver seamless people processes, resolve queries with care and empathy, and navigate challenges effectively will be key to your success in this role. Typical Main Responsibilities in Your Role: • Manage a busy service desk, handling 40-100 queries a week efficiently, effectively and with empathy and professionalism • Be the friendly expert, answering questions and ensuring our people receive timely answers they need on pay, policies, and benefits in a clear, approachable way • Keep our systems and records accurate and up to date • Help run HR processes including preparing monthly starter and leaver lists • Be proactive in suggesting new ideas to improve processes • Respond to external queries including reference requests • Support with reports, data, and projects to help us work more efficiently What We’re Looking For: • Credible HR admin experience with a knack for systems, processes and policies • A natural attention to detail, and care when handling confidential data • Calm and flexible under pressure, with the ability to adapt when things change quickly • A team player who loves building positive relationships • A curious mindset – you’re great at spotting patterns or thinking up simple solutions • A passion for purpose-driven work and willingness to roll up your sleeves • You’ll need the permanent right to work in the UK What’s in it for You? • Shape the way we work: Bring your ideas and help us improve how we do things it’s not all set in stone • Be part of something bigger: Join a supportive team dedicated to making a difference • Enjoy the perks: Competitive salary and a market-leading 7% employer pension contribution • Save on childcare: 70% discount at our nurseries if you have children or grandchildren • Time to recharge: 26 days off a year including Christmas closure, your birthday off plus bank holidays • Feel valued: Wellbeing app, shopping discounts, team events, and more • Grow your HR skills: A great opportunity to deepen your expertise and learn more Interested? If you’ve had experience in HR and looking for a meaningful role in a dynamic, purpose led organisation, we’d love to hear from you! We welcome applications from all backgrounds and are committed to building a diverse and inclusive organisation. Applications are progressed as they come in - don’t wait too long to apply!. eligibility_evidence.text: Manpower are currently seeking an interim Logistics Operations Specialist to work with our global FMCG client, Elida Beauty, renowned for brands such as TIGI, VO5, Toni & Guy, and Brylcreem, and become an integral part of their fast-paced environment. The position is based in Holborn, London. This is a full-time temporary role for 12 months, requiring 37.5 hours per week, Monday to Friday. Compensation for this role is competitive, paying up to £48,000 per annum, pro rata, depending upon experience. The role currently offers a mix of remote and onsite working, subject to adjustment based on business requirements. Key Accountabilities Inbound Transportation Coordinate inbound shipments from suppliers, manufacturing sites, and ports to warehouses or distribution centres. Monitor shipment status and communicate delivery updates to relevant stakeholders. Liaise with freight forwarders, transport providers, and 3PL partners to ensure smooth receipt of goods. Investigate and resolve shipment delays, shortages, damages, or documentation issues. Verify shipping documentation including invoices, packing lists, and delivery notes. Support inventory discrepancy investigations with warehouse and logistics partners. Warehouse Operations Support daily warehouse operations through close coordination with 3PL partners. Monitor inbound receipts, inventory movements, order processing, and dispatch activities. Maintain inventory accuracy through regular reconciliation and stock count support. Track warehouse performance against agreed service levels and KPIs. Participate in operational review meetings and follow up on corrective actions. Support pallet management programs and customer-specific logistics requirements. Ensure adherence to company safety, quality, and operational standards. Outbound Transportation Coordinate customer and distributor deliveries to meet agreed service levels. Monitor carrier performance and delivery execution. Ensure shipping documentation is accurate and completed on time. Investigate delivery exceptions and work with stakeholders to resolve issues. Support urgent order deliveries and customer escalations when required. Customs & Compliance Support import and export documentation processes. Coordinate with customs brokers and freight forwarders to facilitate timely customs clearance. Maintain customs, shipping, and compliance records. Monitor shipment clearance status and proactively escalate potential delays. Ensure compliance with company policies and local regulatory requirements. Repacking/Co-packing Operations Coordinate repacking and co-packing activities with external logistics partners. Monitor inventory availability and material readiness for repack activities. Track order fulfilment and completion against agreed timelines. Communicate operational issues and support resolution with cross-functional teams. Maintain records of repack and co-pack activities. Cost & Invoice Management Support tracking of transportation, warehousing, and logistics-related costs. Validate logistics invoices and ensure timely processing. Assist with freight cost reporting and reconciliation activities. Identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency and reduce costs. Support budget tracking and cost analysis activities as required. Reporting & Performance Monitoring Prepare weekly and monthly logistics performance reports. Monitor and report KPIs including On-Time Delivery (OTD), Inventory Accuracy, Order Fulfilment Performance, Freight Cost Performance, Warehouse Service Levels and Damaged Stock Ratio. Maintain logistics dashboards and operational records. Support data analysis and continuous improvement initiatives. Stakeholder & 3PL Coordination Build effective working relationships with 3PL providers, carriers, freight forwarders, and internal teams. Coordinate issue resolution and escalation where required. Support regular service review meetings with logistics partners. Ensure logistics activities are executed in line with agreed service expectations. Key Requirements Experience in logistics, warehousing, transportation, or supply chain operations, preferably within an FMCG environment. Exposure to customs and international logistics processes, particularly import and export documentation. Experience working with 3PL service providers and transport carriers. Experience in inventory management and order fulfilment processes. Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook. Experience with ERP, WMS, or TMS systems (e.g., SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics). Strong analytical and reporting capabilities. Bachelor's degree or equivalent qualification in Supply Chain, Logistics, Business, or a related field preferred. Additional Information Occasional UK based travel required. If you receive suspicious outreach claiming to be from us, please contact us via the ManpowerGroup website.. Hybrid Temporary Full time

The role involves: ✅ Getting the issues that matter most to local people heard by decision-makers in Westminster. ✅ Delivering creative public affairs campaigns that help us achieve our key missions. ✅ Helping manage high-profile ministerial visits to Islington. ✅ Building relationships with key stakeholders, to help advance our public affairs goals. ✅ Identifying opportunities for the council to meaningfully influence Government consultations and inquiries. To support the delivery of the wider communications service's objectives, giving advice and support on public affairs for major campaigns. The postholder will have lead responsibility and accountability for the following: • Plan and deliver public affairs campaigns for the council, tied to communications priorities and council objectives • Identifying legislative and campaign priorities, tracking Government and other policy development and overseeing the coordination of the council's responses to issues and strategic engagement with MPs • Update and operate a public affairs and policy tracking system, monitoring legislative business and coordinating effective council responses to new legislation, government consultations and Select Committee inquiries with services • Provide advice on public affairs issues to senior officers and councillors • Working with the Digital Communications and Engagement Manager, provide content for social media channels, email marketing, website and instant messaging, as part of integrated campaigns • Contribute towards council print publications, and their associated digital channels • Be an advocate for strategic communications within the council, demonstrating the importance of planned and targeted communications and corporate grip on issues • Ensure public affairs work is driven by research, data and insight, and is culturally competent for Islington's communities The key experiences and skills necessary for the role include: • Experience of delivering public affairs work, ideally in local government or the public sector • Understanding of the legislative process and how policy is developed • Ability to turn complex information into creative, compelling, relevant and targeted content that tells a clear and consistent story to its target audience • Experience of preparing briefings for evidence sessions or media interviews • Experience or a keen interest in working with elected politicians and in a political environment • Experience of tracking and planning work effectively, ideally in a communications or public affairs setting • Proven knowledge and understanding of local government and the challenges it faces • A good understanding of the legislative process and experience of public affairs • Experience of delivering or taking part in communications or public affairs campaigns • Good political awareness and understanding of what drives political priorities and policymaking • Excellent interpersonal, leadership and management skills to motivate colleagues to achieve change and improve services • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, and the ability to motivate, inspire and influence others • Personal and professional demeanour which generates credibility and confidence amongst the general public, members, chief officers, staff, external partners and all other stakeholders • Ability to work under pressure, meeting deadlines and balancing different priorities and workloads • Ability to work collaboratively with a range of internal and external stakeholders • A commitment to cultural competence and understanding of the needs of Islington’s diverse community. Hybrid Temporary Full time

eligibility_evidence.text: Enfield Council's Integrated Community Equipment Service (ICES) is seeking a motivated and customer-focused Community Equipment Officer to support the delivery of essential community equipment to residents across Enfield and neighbouring boroughs. This varied role involves coordinating equipment provision, undertaking equipment assessments, supporting service users and health professionals, maintaining accurate records, and ensuring equipment is delivered, collected and managed efficiently. Working closely with Occupational Therapists, health colleagues, care providers and service users, you will play a key role in helping people maintain their independence, safety and wellbeing within their own homes. Enfield is one of London's most diverse and vibrant boroughs, serving a growing population with a strong commitment to delivering high-quality public services. Our vision is to create a healthier, safer and more inclusive borough where residents can live independently and thrive within their communities. Through partnership working with the NHS and Adult Social Care services, our Integrated Community Equipment Service supports thousands of residents each year by providing timely access to equipment that promotes independence, reduces hospital admissions and supports hospital discharge. We are looking for an organised, flexible and proactive individual with experience of working in health, social care, community equipment services or a customer-focused environment. You will have excellent communication skills, the ability to build positive relationships with a wide range of stakeholders, and a strong commitment to delivering outstanding customer service. The successful candidate will be confident using IT systems, managing competing priorities and working both independently and as part of a team. Knowledge of community equipment, moving and handling equipment, or working with vulnerable adults would be advantageous, although training will be provided for the right candidate. A practical, solution-focused approach and a commitment to improving outcomes for residents are essential. In addition to Enfield Council's comprehensive employee benefits package, we offer the opportunity to join a supportive and dedicated team that makes a genuine difference to residents' lives every day. You will benefit from ongoing training and professional development opportunities, regular supervision and support, flexible working arrangements where service needs allow, and the chance to work within an integrated health and social care environment. This is an excellent opportunity for someone looking to develop their career within community services while contributing to a forward-thinking service focused on independence, prevention and excellent customer outcomes. Contact Details: If you would like to know more about the role, please contact Maurice Needham: [contact email on source] for an informal discussion. If you have any difficulties accessing this information, please contact Vickie McGrath on 0208 132 1053 or at [contact email on source] “This authority is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expects all staff and volunteers to share in this commitment”. We reserve the right to close this vacancy once a sufficient number of applications have been received. Therefore, we advise that you complete fully and submit your application as soon as possible to avoid disappointment. We do not see your name or title when shortlisting your application. This is one of many initiatives to build a more talented and diverse workforce. However, if you put your name on your CV or Statement it will be visible to us. For this reason, we ask that you do not include your name on these documents. Please note it is your responses to the Essential/Desirable criteria, as detailed in the Job Description and Person Specification which is available on the job advert, that will determine if you are shortlisted for an interview, therefore we encourage you to always address the essential and desirable criteria in your application/CV. Why it's great to work for Enfield Council: - An excellent pension through the Local Government Pension Scheme (LGPS). - Up to 32 days annual leave depending on grade and length of service. You will also get eight public holidays per year and an extra day off at Christmas. - A blend of remote and office based working for most roles. - Interest free season ticket loan repayable over three or ten months. - Career development and learning experiences from a range of training courses and learning methods. - Employee Assistance Programme to provide advice and counselling services. This is a free and confidential service available to staff and members of their family. - Health and leisure discounts and tax-free bikes for work. We are passionate about our people and how we deliver services to our community in Enfield. That’s why we encourage a culture that puts our customers at the heart of everything we do - by empowering our people to work together to find solutions, be open, honest and respectful, take responsibility and listen and learn. If you value these behaviours too, we’d love to hear from you - and of course we are always happy to talk flexible working, click here to find out more. If you have previously applied for this role within the past 6 months, unfortunately, a second application will not be considered. Certain posts in the Council are ‘politically restricted’ which means that staff employed in these posts may not undertake political activities either in or outside the workplace and therefore if candidates are affiliated with any political party, we may not be able to proceed with their application.. Permanent Full time

Join our client as a Police Community Support Officer and play a vital role in keeping millions of passengers and staff safe across the UK rail network. PCSOs are an integral part of our client. They carry out vital work across the railway network to keep passengers and staff safe, delivering an exceptional service to their communities across England and Wales. About the Role As a PCSO, you will protect and serve the railway environment, helping to reduce disruption, prevent crime, and improve public confidence. This is a unique and varied role where no two days are the same. You will: - Conduct visible patrols across stations and the rail network. - Support victims and provide reassurance to the public. - Assist with minor investigations and intelligence gathering. - Help manage security threats and incidents. - Build strong relationships within communities and partner organisations. - Support Police Officers in operational policing activity. Unlike many Home Office forces, PCSOs are trained and equipped with handcuffs, giving you an enhanced role within operational policing. What They're Looking For They are seeking individuals who: - Are resilient and calm under pressure. - Demonstrate excellent customer service skills. - Have strong communication and interpersonal ability. - Are passionate about supporting communities and building trust. - Can work effectively as part of a team. You must be prepared to work shifts, including weekends and bank holidays. Locations Our client is recruiting PCSOs within B Division, including locations such as Stratford, Kings Cross, Liverpool Street, Waterloo, Euston and other stations across the network. What you'll get in return: - Salary: £28,486.92 per year - £4,613.61 London allowance - Shift allowance up to 20 percent (minimum 15 percent after training) - 28 days annual leave, rising to 30 with service - Travel benefits - Access to internal progression opportunities, including routes to become a Police Officer - Ongoing learning and development through in-house talent and development teams - Defined contribution pension scheme (administered by Royal London) Eligibility You will not be eligible to apply if: - You have been unsuccessful at interview within the last 3 months for a PCSO role. - You have been unsuccessful in application or online testing within the last 3 months for PCSO, Police Officer or Special Constable roles. - You have failed vetting within the last 12 months. - You have received a custodial or suspended sentence. - You have been dismissed from a police force or are under investigation. - You have a current CCJ, unmanaged IVA or unresolved bankruptcy. - You do not have the right to work in the UK. - You have not lived continuously in the UK for the past three years. - You have tattoos considered offensive (visible tattoos assessed case by case). All cautions, convictions and police involvement must be declared but will be assessed individually. Want To Apply? Applying is straightforward, with all applications completed online. Click apply now and complete your application. As part of the process, you will complete a Situational Judgement Test (SJT). If unsuccessful, you can reapply in three months. Our client encourages you to attend a Recruitment Q&A session before applying to better understand the role. This is an ongoing campaign. Successful applicants will be placed in a 12-month candidate pool and considered for vacancies as they arise.. On-site Permanent Full time
